title: AWS Complete Learning Quiz
description: Test your AWS knowledge across IAM, EC2, VPC, S3, Lambda, and more.

questions.question: In AWS IAM, what takes the highest priority when evaluating permissions?
options: A. Identity-based policies
B. Resource-based policies
C. An explicit Deny statement in any policy
D. AWS managed policies
questions.explain: An explicit Deny always overrides any Allow in IAM policy evaluation, regardless of where it comes from.

questions.question: What is the difference between IAM roles and IAM users?
options: A. Roles are for humans; users are for services
B. Roles provide temporary credentials assumed by AWS services/users; users have permanent credentials
C. Users can have multiple roles simultaneously; roles can only have one user
D. Roles are global; users are region-specific
questions.explain: Roles are assumed for short-lived, auto-rotating credentials, while IAM users hold long-term access keys or passwords.

questions.question: An EC2 instance in a private subnet needs to download OS updates. What AWS resource enables this?
options: A. Internet Gateway
B. Virtual Private Gateway
C. NAT Gateway (in a public subnet)
D. VPC Endpoint
questions.explain: A NAT Gateway in a public subnet lets private-subnet instances reach the internet outbound while staying unreachable from it.

questions.question: What does S3 'versioning' protect against?
options: A. Unauthorized access to bucket objects
B. Accidental deletion or overwriting of objects — keeps all versions
C. Cross-region data transfer costs
D. Object size limits
questions.explain: Versioning keeps every prior copy of an object, so overwrites or deletes can be undone by restoring an earlier version.

questions.question: Which EC2 pricing model offers the greatest discount (up to 90%) but can be interrupted?
options: A. Reserved Instances
B. Dedicated Hosts
C. Spot Instances
D. Savings Plans
questions.explain: Spot Instances use spare AWS capacity at steep discounts but can be reclaimed with short notice, suiting fault-tolerant workloads.

questions.question: What is the difference between RDS Multi-AZ and Read Replicas?
options: A. Multi-AZ is for disaster recovery (standby replica, synchronous, no reads); Read Replicas are for read scaling (asynchronous)
B. Multi-AZ allows read traffic; Read Replicas do not
C. Multi-AZ uses asynchronous replication; Read Replicas use synchronous
D. They are the same feature with different names
questions.explain: Multi-AZ keeps a synchronous standby purely for failover, while Read Replicas use async replication to offload read traffic.

questions.question: What is a VPC endpoint used for?
options: A. Connecting VPCs to the internet
B. Allowing VPC resources to access AWS services privately without routing traffic through the internet
C. Establishing VPN connections to on-premises networks
D. Exposing internal services to the internet
questions.explain: VPC endpoints let resources reach AWS services like S3 or DynamoDB over AWS's private network instead of the public internet.

questions.question: In AWS Lambda, what causes a 'cold start'?
options: A. Running a Lambda function for the first time ever
B. Lambda spinning up a new execution environment when no warm instance is available
C. A Lambda function that takes more than 30 seconds to execute
D. Exceeding the concurrent execution limit
questions.explain: A cold start happens when Lambda must provision and initialize a fresh execution environment rather than reuse a warm one.

questions.question: What is the maximum retention period for S3 Glacier Deep Archive?
options: A. 90 days
B. 1 year
C. 7 years
D. No maximum — you set the retention period
questions.explain: S3 Glacier Deep Archive has no fixed maximum retention; you define storage duration based on your compliance or archival needs.

questions.question: Which DynamoDB feature allows reading data at its most recent state, even in a multi-writer scenario?
options: A. Eventually consistent reads (default)
B. Strongly consistent reads
C. Transactional reads
D. DynamoDB Streams
questions.explain: Strongly consistent reads return the most up-to-date data reflecting all successful writes, unlike eventually consistent reads.

questions.question: What is AWS GuardDuty?
options: A. A firewall for EC2 instances
B. A threat detection service that continuously monitors AWS accounts using ML and threat intelligence
C. A web application firewall (WAF)
D. An identity governance service
questions.explain: GuardDuty continuously analyzes logs like VPC Flow Logs, DNS, and CloudTrail with ML and threat intel to detect malicious activity.

questions.question: In S3, what is the purpose of a presigned URL?
options: A. Permanently makes an S3 object public
B. Grants temporary, time-limited access to a private S3 object without requiring AWS credentials
C. Signs an S3 bucket policy cryptographically
D. Creates a signed version of the S3 bucket name
questions.explain: A presigned URL embeds a signature granting temporary access to a specific object without the requester needing AWS credentials.

questions.question: What is the difference between an ALB and NLB?
options: A. ALB operates at Layer 7 (HTTP) with path/host routing; NLB at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) with ultra-low latency
B. ALB is for internal traffic; NLB is for internet-facing
C. ALB supports WebSocket; NLB does not
D. ALB can have static IPs; NLB cannot
questions.explain: ALB works at the application layer for HTTP/HTTPS routing rules, while NLB works at the transport layer for extreme performance.

questions.question: What is AWS KMS envelope encryption?
options: A. Encrypting data with multiple CMKs simultaneously
B. Using a CMK to encrypt a data key, then using the data key to encrypt actual data — CMK never leaves KMS
C. Wrapping encryption keys in an envelope for transit
D. A method to encrypt KMS keys with other KMS keys
questions.explain: Envelope encryption uses a CMK to encrypt a data key that encrypts your data, so the CMK itself never leaves KMS.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an IAM permissions boundary?
options: A. Sets the maximum permissions an IAM entity can have — even if identity policies grant more, boundary limits them
B. Creates a firewall around IAM users
C. Defines minimum permissions required for an AWS account
D. Restricts which regions an IAM user can access
questions.explain: A permissions boundary caps the maximum permissions an entity can ever receive, even if its identity policies grant more.

questions.question: Which AWS service would you use to automatically rotate database credentials?
options: A. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
B. AWS Secrets Manager
C. AWS KMS
D. AWS IAM
questions.explain: AWS Secrets Manager natively supports automatic, scheduled rotation of database credentials via Lambda rotation functions.

questions.question: What is DynamoDB's RCU consumption for 1 strongly consistent read of a 7KB item?
options: A. 1 RCU
B. 2 RCU
C. 3.5 RCU
D. 7 RCU
questions.explain: One strongly consistent read uses 1 RCU per 4KB, so a 7KB item rounds up to two 4KB units, consuming 2 RCU.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an SCP (Service Control Policy) in AWS Organizations?
options: A. Encrypts data across all accounts in the organization
B. Sets maximum permission guardrails for member accounts — even if identity policies allow, SCP can deny
C. Manages service quotas across the organization
D. Controls which AWS services are available per region
questions.explain: SCPs set organization-wide permission guardrails, denying actions for member accounts even when their own IAM policies allow them.

questions.question: Which Route 53 routing policy routes based on the health of your endpoints with an active-passive failover?
options: A. Latency routing
B. Weighted routing
C. Failover routing
D. Geolocation routing
questions.explain: Failover routing sends traffic to a primary resource and switches to a standby only when health checks mark the primary unhealthy.

questions.question: What is IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) in EKS?
options: A. An IAM role that only allows read access to S3
B. A mechanism that lets Kubernetes pods assume IAM roles via service account annotations, avoiding node-level permissions
C. Identity-based Resource Scheduling Algorithm
D. An AWS service for managing Kubernetes RBAC
questions.explain: IRSA maps a Kubernetes service account to an IAM role via OIDC federation, giving pods fine-grained AWS permissions per workload.

questions.question: What is the purpose of CloudFront origin access control (OAC)?
options: A. Controls which origins CloudFront can access on the internet
B. Ensures only CloudFront can access S3 objects — blocks direct S3 URL access
C. Provides access control for CloudFront admin console
D. Controls edge location selection for caching
questions.explain: OAC lets only CloudFront sign requests to a private S3 bucket, preventing users from bypassing CloudFront via direct S3 URLs.

questions.question: In AWS, what is the Shared Responsibility Model for EC2 instances?
options: A. AWS manages everything including the OS
B. AWS manages hypervisor and physical infrastructure; customer manages guest OS, patches, apps, and security groups
C. Customer manages hardware; AWS manages software
D. Both AWS and customer share equal responsibility for all layers
questions.explain: AWS secures the hardware and hypervisor layer, while the customer is responsible for the guest OS, patching, apps, and security groups.

questions.question: What does Aurora's 'cluster endpoint' route traffic to?
options: A. All Aurora instances randomly
B. Only read replicas
C. The primary (writer) instance
D. The instance with lowest latency from the client
questions.explain: The cluster endpoint always points to the current primary writer instance, ensuring writes go to the correct Aurora node.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group?
options: A. Guaranteed availability with no interruptions
B. Up to 90% cost reduction for fault-tolerant workloads that can handle interruptions
C. Faster instance startup compared to On-Demand
D. Free egress data transfer
questions.explain: Spot Instances in Auto Scaling groups cut compute costs up to 90% for workloads resilient to interruption, like batch processing.

questions.question: What AWS service provides a centralized view of security findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and others?
options: A. AWS CloudTrail
B. AWS Config
C. AWS Security Hub
D. Amazon Detective
questions.explain: AWS Security Hub aggregates and prioritizes findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and other services into one dashboard.

questions.question: What is the 'Strangler Fig' pattern used for when migrating a monolith to microservices?
options: A. Rewriting the entire monolith from scratch before any migration begins
B. Gradually routing new/refactored functionality through a facade to new microservices while the monolith keeps serving everything else, until it's fully replaced
C. Running two completely separate monoliths in parallel forever
D. A database migration technique unrelated to application architecture
questions.explain: The Strangler Fig pattern migrates incrementally — a facade (API Gateway/proxy) routes traffic to new microservices piece by piece while the monolith still handles everything else, avoiding a risky big-bang rewrite.

questions.question: In CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation), why are the write model and read model kept separate?
options: A. To save on database licensing costs
B. So the write side can stay simple and consistent while the read side can be denormalized and shaped exactly for fast, query-specific access patterns
C. Because AWS requires separate databases for reads and writes
D. To make the application harder to test
questions.explain: CQRS separates commands (writes) from queries (reads) so each side can be optimized independently — the write model stays normalized/consistent, while the read model can be denormalized for whatever query patterns (dashboards, search) actually need.

questions.question: What does Event Sourcing store, as opposed to traditional CRUD?
options: A. Only the current state of each record, like normal CRUD
B. The full sequence of events that led to the current state, so state can be reconstructed by replaying history
C. A compressed binary snapshot updated nightly
D. Only error events, not successful state changes
questions.explain: Event Sourcing persists every event (OrderCreated, ItemAdded, etc.) rather than just current state — current state is derived by replaying the event log, which gives a full audit trail and the ability to rebuild any past state.

questions.question: What problem does the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) API Gateway pattern solve?
options: A. It eliminates the need for authentication entirely
B. It provides a dedicated gateway per client type (web, mobile) that shapes/aggregates responses for that client's specific needs, instead of one generic API serving everyone
C. It automatically scales the database behind the API
D. It replaces the need for an API Gateway entirely
questions.explain: BFF gives each client type (web, iOS, Android) its own tailored gateway/API shape, avoiding a one-size-fits-all API that over- or under-fetches data for different clients.

questions.question: In the worked URL shortener design, why is read traffic cached aggressively with ElastiCache?
options: A. Because writes are far more frequent than reads in this system
B. Because redirects (reads) vastly outnumber new short-URL creations (writes) — roughly 10:1 in the example — so caching the hot subset of URLs removes most load from the database
C. Caching is required by AWS for all DynamoDB tables
D. To avoid having to generate base62 codes
questions.explain: URL shorteners are extremely read-heavy (redirects happen far more often than new links are created), so caching the popular subset of mappings in ElastiCache removes the vast majority of load from the database.

questions.question: What is the key operational difference between target tracking, step scaling, and scheduled scaling in AWS Auto Scaling?
options: A. They all do exactly the same thing with different names

B. Target tracking maintains a metric at a set value automatically, step scaling adds different capacity based on alarm severity, and scheduled scaling triggers scaling at known times regardless of current metrics
C. Scheduled scaling is the only one that can scale down
D. Step scaling only works with Spot Instances
questions.explain: Target tracking is 'set and forget' (hold a metric near a target), step scaling applies proportionally larger responses to more severe alarm breaches, and scheduled scaling scales at predetermined times for predictable traffic patterns — each suits a different scenario.

questions.question: Why does horizontal scaling require an application to be stateless?
options: A. Stateless apps use less CPU per request

B. If session/state data lives in an individual instance's memory, requests routed to a different instance won't see that data — state must live in a shared store (Redis/DynamoDB) so any instance can serve any request
C. AWS Auto Scaling Groups only support stateless applications by license agreement
D. Stateless applications don't need load balancers
questions.explain: Horizontal scaling adds/removes instances dynamically — if a user's session data were stored only in one instance's memory, a request landing on a different instance would lose that context, so state must be externalized to something all instances can reach.

questions.question: What is the key difference between AWS Savings Plans and Reserved Instances?
options: A. They offer identical discounts and flexibility, just different names

B. Savings Plans commit to a $/hour spend and apply automatically across instance families/regions; Reserved Instances commit to a specific instance type/region, offering similar discounts with less flexibility
C. Reserved Instances only work for RDS, Savings Plans only work for EC2
D. Savings Plans require a 3-year minimum commitment
questions.explain: Savings Plans commit to a dollar-per-hour spend level and apply broadly across instance families and regions automatically, while Reserved Instances lock in a specific instance configuration — similar discount depth, but Savings Plans trade a bit of discount ceiling for much more flexibility.

questions.question: What does AWS Cost Anomaly Detection do?
options: A. It automatically cancels any resource that costs more than $100
B. It builds an ML baseline of normal spend patterns per service/account and alerts when actual spend deviates unusually from that pattern
C. It only detects anomalies in EC2 CPU usage, not cost
D. It requires manually setting a fixed dollar threshold for every service
questions.explain: Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to learn what 'normal' spend looks like for your account/service and flags statistically unusual deviations automatically, without requiring a manually-tuned fixed threshold.

questions.question: Where does the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) land, and how is it typically queried for FinOps analysis?
options: A. It only exists as a PDF emailed monthly to the billing contact
B. It lands in an S3 bucket as detailed line-item data, commonly queried with Athena and visualized in QuickSight
C. It's only accessible through AWS Support tickets
D. It's automatically deleted after 24 hours
questions.explain: The CUR delivers the most granular billing data available (every line item, hourly) to an S3 bucket, which FinOps teams typically query with Athena (SQL over S3 data) and visualize in QuickSight or similar BI tools.
